_comment: The GPU fleet: every host and card, with the host's admission rules. DATA, read by scripts/lib/gpu_fleet.py (claims, windows, admission, board, the guard) and by `dreamteam gpu run`. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-29-gpu-fleet-design.md. Sizes marked in `measured` were read with an instrument (nvidia-smi / free / /proc/swaps / df / lspci over ssh); change a size only from a new measurement, and say when. `dreamteam gpu inventory --check` re-measures and reports drift.
measured: 2026-09-29 09:1x PDT by cirrus-scry: nvidia-smi --query-gpu, free -m, /proc/swaps, df -BG /, nproc, lspci -vv (B60 BAR2)

_notes.cap_margin: cap = measured peak x 1.2 for fixed-shape jobs (FAMILIAR-RULES rule 3: 'measured peak plus 20%'; stage2_train's peaks are stable across runs).
_notes.grows_margin: x 1.5 for any job whose memory grows with run length (caches, arenas, variable-length inputs). FAMILIAR-RULES amendment 2026-09-28 23:4x-23:5x after two OOM kills: Canary-1B's arena (a 2-clip 4.75 GB peak + 20% = 6 GB; the full run passed 6.26 GB) and the lidar build's GDAL block cache.
_notes.vram_margin_mib: claimed VRAM on a card must leave 1 GiB (guest_run.sh: GPU free >= cap + 1 GB).
_notes.refuse_exit: 75 = EX_TEMPFAIL, retry later: the code all three GEMS launchers already use for an admission refusal.

guard._comment: The launch guard (scripts/gpu-guard.sh, scripts/lib/gpu_detect.py). A launch is recognised where a shell RUNS it, never where it is mentioned. python counts only with GPU evidence: a CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES or ZE_AFFINITY_MASK index, --device cuda[:N], a GPU launcher, torchrun/deepspeed/accelerate launch, or a script whose basename matches gpu_programs. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= (empty) or -1, or --device cpu, marks a job CPU-only. A GPU program missing here still shows on the board as IN USE, NO CLAIM: add it here.
guard._classes: morpheus-gems 12:1x 09-29: gpu_scripts are GEMS wrappers whose child is stage2_train.py (judged as GPU by the parent; used when the script cannot be read, e.g. run on gpu0 over ssh); b60_bench.sh is drift's torch.xpu bench on the Arc B60 (kind xpu: familiar:xpu0, claimable once compute_ok is set after the ReBAR reboot); cpu_programs are CPU-only and never a launch, whatever the environment says.
